amends.clause: design.artifacts 1 — the manifest item "repair's frozen max_rounds"
amends.frozenTextVerbatim: evidence/<run_id>.b12.tasks.json — committed BEFORE the first billed request, as an ancestor of everything downstream, carrying: 30 ordered task ids; per task the prompt text and its sha256, the base commit SHA, the exact verification command string(s), the frozen gate `category`, repair's frozen max_rounds, the acceptance predicate and expected exit code, the declared verification stratum and expected subagent stratum, and the file scope; ...
amends.theGapInOneSentence: Artifact 1 requires the manifest to CARRY repair's frozen max_rounds. No clause requires an observation to RUN under it, and voidConditions 4 does not reach the case: 4 fires when a frozen item CHANGES, and a session calling repair at another value changes nothing — the manifest still declares what it declared.

scope: PROSPECTIVE. This amendment governs every B12 run whose FIRST SCORED OBSERVATION is committed after the commit that introduces this artifact. It governs no earlier run and may not be applied retroactively.
effect: For a governed run: VOID if any ASSESSED observation's scoped repair telemetry carries a detail.max_rounds different from that task's frozen repairMaxRounds, or carries no numeric detail.max_rounds at all. CORRECTED 2026-08-14 by review: this read 'any scored observation OWNED repair telemetry', and neither word survived the code. The offender set is assessed.filter(a => a.repairRounds.length > 0) (assemble.ts:1392) — EVERY assessed observation, whatever its disposition, not only the scored ones; a void or excluded observation offends this clause exactly as a scored one does. 'OWNED' is replaced by 'scoped' because the rows are not the observation's private log but scopeTelemetry's narrowing (assemble.ts:688) of the run-wide union (assemble.ts:282), which is a different set — see whatItDoesNotClose on the two detectors. It is a RUN-LEVEL archive check named "amendment 2026-08-14 — repair frozen max_rounds", NOT a disposition. CORRECTED 2026-08-14 AFTER THE WIRING: this field first said "the disposition name is void(condition_not_as_registered)", and the implementation deliberately did not create one. Adding a disposition would have meant a new member of the closed precedence list, and worse, a per-observation verdict — the exclusion route this amendment exists to avoid. A run-level check needs no new name at all: every observation keeps the disposition it had, and what dies is the run.
whyRunLevelAndNotAnExclusion: voidConditions 9 already settled this trade in the frozen text and states its own ground: it is 'run-level, so triggering it costs the run rather than buying an exclusion'. The same reasoning binds here and more sharply. repair is a TREATMENT-ONLY tool, so an exclusion rule would drop only treatment observations, the next task in the committed order would take the vacated admission slot, and whether the dropped tasks carry higher or lower savings than their replacements is unmeasured and unmeasurable before the run. That is a selection channel into the admitted set whose SIGN cannot be established, bought in exchange for a check. Run-level kills both arms together and selects on nothing.
whyFailClosedOnAnAbsentField: A repair row carrying no numeric detail.max_rounds cannot be compared, and 'cannot tell' may not wear the same answer as 'matched' — the failure b12-scorer-mac.sh already voids on as limits-unverifiable. The field has existed since the telemetry detail was added; a row without it is a row from somewhere else, or from a build this run may not be scored against.
reason: Found 2026-08-14 by adversarial review, pre-data. repairMaxRounds was refused when absent (b12-manifest.mjs:457), carried into the manifest (:480) and archived (archive.ts:256) — and then nothing transmitted or checked it. The observation session is handed task.prompt alone (b12-run.mjs), no corpus prompt mentions repair at all, and an observation matched the declared 3 only by COINCIDENCE of the tool's own default. A session calling max_rounds: 10 archived clean, and the only detail.max_rounds comparisons in the repository were unit tests of the tool itself. A frozen item nothing can violate is not frozen; it is decorative. This amendment supplies the sentence the frozen text does not carry.
whyNotDeliveredInstead: The obvious repair — tell the session the number — is refused on purpose. The prompt is frozen by its own promptSha256 and the per-arm policy arrives from the committed out-of-repo blob, so delivering the limit would move the experiment's INPUT in order to satisfy a check on its output, and no arm's transcript would afterwards be comparable with one recorded before. Verification reads what happened; delivery changes what happens. Only the first is available to an amendment.
whatItDoesNotClose: A repair call whose telemetry row never landed. The writer swallows append failures by design (src/telemetry.ts), and capture publishes invocationsWithoutRow as REPORTED, DECIDING NOTHING with a lawful counter-example beside it: a tool whose PREFLIGHT refuses emits no row while its result still sits in the transcript, so 'every local invocation has a row' is FALSE on a path the design intends. ABSENCE OF A ROW IS THEREFORE NOT EVIDENCE OF COMPLIANCE, and this amendment is evaluated over rows that exist and over nothing else. A guard built on the contrary premise would void lawful observations, which is why none is proposed.

The scope of what the driver reads. archive.telemetry is every parseable row in the observation's own worktree log up to the acceptance boundary (capture.ts:561); it is NOT the scoped subset scoring computes with scopeTelemetry (assemble.ts:658). Each observation gets a fresh worktree, so a foreign row must be written into that private tree to appear at all — but if one is, this amendment can void a run on a row scoring would have excluded as foreign.

The delivery gap itself. Nothing instructs the session to pass the frozen value; compliance is still reached by the tool's default happening to equal it. This amendment makes disobedience fatal to the run. It does not make obedience instructed, and a future change to DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS would silently make every compliant session non-compliant.

budget_seconds, which remains an unregistered free parameter (F7). Nothing freezes it, so there is no declared value to compare against, and this amendment does not create one — inventing a number here would register a condition by side effect, which is the defect it exists to answer, not to repeat.

CLOSED 2026-08-14, and kept here because this file does not rewrite what it once asserted. This item read: 'An unaskable git history. audit.ts introducingCommit maps a FAILED git log and a file with no introducing commit to the same null (:1215-1220), and both then read as governs=false — so a repository the audit cannot interrogate silently runs the pre-amendment regime. Inherited from the conformance-paths amendment, which is decided by the same helper, and named here rather than repaired: distinguishing the two cases changes a shared function that another amendment depends on, and that is its own pre-data change with its own review.' That review was run and the change made in the same pass: introducingCommit and lastCommit now return a discriminated answer, a FAILED log raises AuditRefused at all six call sites, and a log that succeeds with no lines still means 'no introducing commit' and still reads as not-governing. Both controls ship in tests/b12-audit.test.ts. The conformance-paths amendment is hardened by the same change, as this item predicted it would be.

Agreement between the two detectors, which do NOT stand in a containment relation. CORRECTED 2026-08-14, same day, by adversarial review: this item first read 'Driver is a superset of scorer, always, so the disagreement is one-directional — the driver can warn where this clause stays silent and can never be silent where it fires.' Both halves are false. The driver-side twin in scripts/b12-run.mjs reads one worktree's own log; this clause reads the run-wide union of every valid treatment observation's identified rows (assemble.ts:282) narrowed by scopeTelemetry (assemble.ts:688). The two scoping axes are INDEPENDENT, so each set holds rows the other does not: driver-only, a foreign row written into that private worktree that is neither a known invocation nor inside the window; scorer-only, a row archived by another treatment observation whose timestamp lands in this transcript's ±60 s window or whose invocation id it recognises. THE DRIVER CAN THEREFORE BE SILENT ON A ROW THAT VOIDS THE RUN, and an operator may not read its silence as this clause's assent. Still deliberate, for the reason that survives: narrowing the driver would hide from the operator the stray rows they are the only one positioned to explain.
doesNotChange: the frozen pre-registration artifact, which is NOT edited — its sha256 pin stands
the outcome, the 30%/15% bands, the unit definition, the admission rule, the metric arithmetic, the acceptance predicates, the two sealed manifests

the 23 existing voidConditions, none of which is widened, narrowed or re-ordered, AND the closed disposition precedence list, which gains no member — this adds a RUN-LEVEL archive check, not a disposition. CORRECTED 2026-08-14: this line first read "this adds a disposition, it does not edit one", which the wiring made false.
the committed order, the admission cap of 20, or which attempt scores

stateAtWriting.note: Written before the harness seal and before any registration, so no B12 residual exists to select against. It is nevertheless POST-FREEZE and must always be described as such: a governed run is governed by the 2026-08-05 pre-registration PLUS this artifact, never by the pre-registration alone.

enforcedBy: src/cost/b12/audit.ts computes whether this amendment governs — its INTRODUCING commit against the run freeze anchor, the same prospective test the conformance-paths amendment gets — and publishes path, commit, sha256 and governs on the audit artifact flat input face, so which regime produced a verdict is readable from the artifact rather than inferred. src/cost/b12/assemble.ts owns the clause, reads that answer off the committed audit and never re-derives it, and raises a RUN-LEVEL archive check named "amendment 2026-08-14 — repair frozen max_rounds". A fired archive check replaces the arithmetic verdict with void and names the clause, which emit.ts then writes and prints. No observation disposition or admission changes: the clause is run-level and selects on nothing.
sealingPrecondition: SATISFIED ON ITS OWN TERMS as of 2026-08-14, and the wording that follows is the record of what was required rather than a claim to have exceeded it. The enforcement exists, and the negative control shows the void FIRING on a fabricated mismatch (tests/b12-assemble.test.ts) against a positive control on the same fixture at the frozen value. The governance gate is bound in three regimes — governs, does not govern, and no committed audit — and the last of those is now also carried in uncheckedClauses, so a run whose audit predates these keys cannot be published FINAL over a rule nobody established. WHAT A SEAL STILL REQUIRES, unchanged: that this file own no dead letter. Re-read enforcedBy against the code before registering, because the first attempt at wiring computed the facts and never serialised them — the rule could not fire on any real run, and the test did not catch it because it supplied the audit inputs by hand.
reportedBesideIt: observation.repairRoundsFindings is written on EVERY observation, governed or not, scored or pilot. On an ungoverned run those findings are REPORTED, DECIDING NOTHING, and may never be invoked to void or rescue it — they exist so that a reader can see a condition breach the amendment's clock does not reach.
adjudication: docs/b12-scorer/FINDINGS.md and b12-corpus/manifest-config.json — the 2026-08-14 adversarial review of 8fedebc, whose third finding this answers
separateOnPurpose: Committed alone. The conformance-paths amendment and the platform amendment still owed are distinct pre-data amendments and must not be folded into this one, nor it into them.
